title: Positive depth implies an internal gate
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number and let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables. If the depth of $c$ is at least $1$, then there are a Boolean gate type and a list of child circuits such that $c$ is the node formed from that gate type and those children.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables
replaced:
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit whose depth is at least $1$. Then $c$ is not a literal: it
is an internal gate, so there exist a Boolean flag $\mathit{isAnd}$ and a list $cs$ of
child circuits for which $c$ is the node with gate type $\mathit{isAnd}$ applied to the
children $cs$.
